issues.legal_issue: The annual value of a building that has never been let and for which standard rent has not been fixed may be assessed by a reasonable criterion that does not follow the rent-control standard-rent provisions.
material_facts: The building had never been let and was operated as a hotel by its owners.
No standard rent had been fixed, and the question of fixing standard rent did not arise.
The municipal authority determined annual value using a criterion other than the standard-rent provisions.
issues.conclusion: The municipal authority was entitled to determine the building’s reasonable letting value without being bound by the standard-rent provisions.
issues.legal_principle: Section 138(b) of the Madhya Pradesh Municipal Corporation Act, 1956 requires annual value to be based on the gross annual rent reasonably expected at the time of assessment, while its non-obstante clause permits departure from other laws. Where standard rent has been fixed and there is no fraud or collusion, it represents the reasonable letting value; where it has not been fixed and the question of fixing it does not arise, another suitable criterion may be used without regard to section 7 of the Madhya Pradesh Accommodation Control Act, 1961. Corporation of Calcutta v. Smt. Padma Debi, Corporation of Calcutta v. Life Insurance Corporation of India, Guntur Municipal Council v. Guntur Town Rate Payers’ Association, and New Delhi Municipal Committee v. M.N. Soi were distinguished because they concerned rented premises or statutes without the same non-obstante clause.

rule.if: property_tax_assessment_dispute and building_never_let and standard_rent_not_fixed and standard_rent_question_does_not_arise

predicates.property_tax_assessment_dispute: A municipal authority is determining a building’s value for property-tax assessment.
predicates.building_never_let: The building has never been let to a tenant.
predicates.standard_rent_not_fixed: No standard rent has been fixed for the building.
predicates.standard_rent_question_does_not_arise: The circumstances are such that fixing standard rent for the building does not arise.
predicates.assessment_may_use_another_reasonable_cr: The assessing authority may determine annual value using another suitable reasonable criterion.

issues.definition: When a property-tax assessment concerns a never-let building for which standard rent has not been fixed and does not arise, the assessing authority may use another reasonable criterion to determine annual value.

issues.legal_issue: A building’s annual-value assessment is not shown to be procedurally defective for lack of a hearing or an principled basis when the owner had an adequate opportunity to present the case and relevant circumstances were considered.
material_facts: The owner was given ample opportunity by the municipal commissioner to present the objection to the assessment.
The assessment officer considered the relevant circumstances bearing on the building’s reasonable letting value.
The appellate judge found that the hearing was adequate and relevant factors had been considered; the owner did not pursue those objections before the Supreme Court.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in finding that the owner had not received a full hearing or that the valuation was based on no principle.
issues.legal_principle: The record showed an adequate opportunity to make representations and consideration of the relevant circumstances. On those facts, the High Court’s contrary procedural findings were not supported by the record.

predicates.property_tax_assessment_challenge: An owner challenges the procedure or basis used to determine a building’s annual value for property-tax assessment.
predicates.owner_given_adequate_opportunity: The owner was given an adequate opportunity to present the case to the assessing authority.
predicates.relevant_circumstances_considered: The assessing authority considered the circumstances relevant to determining reasonable letting value.
predicates.assessment_not_invalid_for_lack_of_heari: The assessment is not invalid on the grounds that the owner lacked a hearing or that the valuation lacked a principled basis.

issues.definition: When an owner challenges a property-tax assessment but had an adequate opportunity to present the case and relevant circumstances were considered, the assessment is not invalid for lack of a hearing or principle.
